summary: Yiu Wing Chan worked in Buddhist studies. He earned his PhD from the University of Hong Kong by 2013, studying under doctoral supervisor K. L. Dhammajoti.

Yoel Hoffmann (1937–2023) worked in philosophy, Buddhist studies, and Japanology. He studied at Tel Aviv University, Hanazono University under Sojo Hirano and Ben-Ami Scharfstein, and earned a PhD from Kyoto University. He was a professor at the University of Haifa (~1983–2003).
Yohei Furukawa is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied under Ryuji Hayashi and served as an associate professor at Soka University (attested 2026).
Yoichi Fukuda specializes in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He served as a full-time researcher at Toyo Bunko (attested 1986–1991) and as a professor at Otani University (attested 2003 and 2015).

Yongey Mingyur Rinpoche (born 1975) is active in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied at Palpung Sherabling Monastery and Dzongsar Institute under numerous masters, including Nyoshul Khenpo Jamyang Dorje and Tulku Urgyen Rinpoche, becoming abbot of Palpung Sherabling Monastery around 1998.
Yongshan He works in Buddhist studies and religious studies. He studied at McMaster University, where he was supervised by James A. Benn and also studied under Shayne Clarke and Mark Rowe.

Yongtong Tang (1893–1964) was a scholar of Buddhist studies, philosophy, and Indology. Educated at Tsinghua and Harvard under Irving Babbitt and Charles Rockwell Lanman, he taught at Southeast, Nankai, and National Central universities before serving as professor and vice-president at Peking University.

Yoshiaki Shimizu (1936–2021) specialized in Japanology and Buddhist studies. After studying at Harvard University (~1969–1974), he held positions at the University of California, Berkeley (~1975–1979) and served as a professor at Princeton University (~1984–2009).

Yoshifumi Honjo (born 1951) is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology educated at Kyoto University. He held academic posts at Kobe Women's University (1989–2004), Bukkyo University (1980, 2004, 2010, 2014), and Otani University (~1999–2017).

Yoshifumi Mizuno (born 1958) works in Indology and linguistics. He graduated from Tokyo University of Foreign Studies and the University of Tokyo, later serving as an assistant at the University of Tokyo (1986–1992) and associate professor at TUFS (2000–2024).

Yoshihide Yoshizu (1943–2014) worked in Buddhist studies and Sinology. He earned his doctorate at Komazawa University, studying under Shoson Miyamoto and Shigeo Kamata, and served at Komazawa as a lecturer from 1971 and professor from 2001.

Yoshihiko Amino (1929–2004) was a historian and Japanologist. He studied at the University of Tokyo (~1947–1950) and later held posts at Nagoya University (~1967–1980) and Kanagawa University (~1980–2000).

Yoshihiko Nasu specializes in Buddhist studies and Indology. He served as a part-time lecturer at Ryukoku University (attested 2007) and held leadership roles at Kongozyushinkai and Kongozyu (attested 2017).

Yoshihiko Sakurai specializes in Buddhist studies. He pursued doctoral studies at Ryukoku University (attested 2001) and later served there as a part-time lecturer and as a researcher at the Jodo Shinshu Hongwanji-ha Kyogaku Dendo Kenkyu Center (attested 2003).
Yoshihiro Hayashi works in philosophy and Buddhist studies. He served as a part-time lecturer at both Ritsumeikan University and Shitennoji University (attested 2009).

Yoshihito Muroji works in Buddhist studies and Indology. He earned his PhD from the University of Hamburg under Lambert Schmithausen, was an assistant at Kyoto University, an associate professor at Koyasan University (1995–2012), and a professor at Shiga University of Medical Science (2014–2015).
Yoshiki Motoaki is a Buddhist studies scholar who held academic appointments at Otani University, attested in 2013 and 2026.

Yoshimi Nozawa specializes in Buddhist studies and Sinology. As of 2026, he is attested as a part-time lecturer at both the International College for Postgraduate Buddhist Studies and the International Institute for Buddhist Studies.

Yoshinobu Kimoto (born 1950) specializes in history and Japanology. Educated at Komazawa, Meiji, and Tezukayama universities, he served at Yamagata Prefectural Yonezawa Women's Junior College (1993–2000), was president of Koshien Junior College (2000–2012), and professor at Ryukoku University (2013–2021).

Yoshinobu Sakade (1934–2020) was a scholar of Sinology and philosophy. He studied at Kyoto University (~1956–1960) under Mitsuji Fukunaga (~1960–1966) and held an academic post at Kansai University (~1974–2004).
